title: The computed gap between 1/2 and 7/12, and what it is not
body:
## Note

An exhaustive computation over all cyclically reduced homologically trivial words
of length at most 20 in F_2 -- 185,502 symmetry classes -- found no value of scl
anywhere in the open interval (1/2, 7/12). The value 7/12 first occurs at length
12, realised by the word `aaabaBAAbAAB`, and by eight classes at length 20 alone.

This is consistent with the gap suggested in Heuer's survey *What is stable
commutator length?*, and is the strongest direct numerical evidence for it known
to this project.

Two statements are easy to conflate here, and they are about different things.

A **gap** between 1/2 and 7/12 says that both endpoints are attained and nothing
lies between them. An **accumulation point** at 3/4 says that values pile up there,
and that below 3/4 the spectrum is discrete. Neither implies the other.

The word `aaabaBAAbAAB` witnesses both, and that is not a coincidence. It is the
n = 3 member of the family with scl(w_n) = 3/4 - 1/(2n), and 7/12 = 3/4 - 1/6 is
simply the first member of that family exceeding 1/2. The gap (1/2, 7/12) is
exactly the statement that nothing gets between the n = 2 and n = 3 members.

Related work above this in the literature: Heuer, *Gaps in scl for amalgamated free
products and RAAGs* (arXiv:1802.01107, GAFA 2019), a sharp gap of 1/2; Chen-Heuer,
*Spectral gap of scl in graphs of groups and 3-manifolds* (arXiv:1910.14146), a
universal 1/12; Heuer, *The full spectrum of scl on recursively presented groups*
(arXiv:1909.01309).

The numbers here come from a computation carried out in an AI agent session in
August 2026 using `scallop`, in its rigorous exact-rational mode, and spot-checked
against two independent algorithms. **No person has checked it.** Treat it as
computational evidence and not as established fact.
